name: combobox-field
title: Combobox field
summary: Lets people find one value by typing, as a field of a form: a combobox — a box with a list of options that narrows as they type, or, where the product allows it, a value of their own — under a label that can say the field is required or optional, with a line of help and the reason a value was refused.

anatomy.description: The Field: the label row with its glyph and its requirement mark, and the supporting row with the help and the error text. In a look whose combobox floats the label it draws no label row.

The combobox, as the Field's one control: the box and the text typed in it, the leading glyph, the clear button and the chevron, the list with its options, groups and status row, and the label that floats in the box in the looks that float one.

props.name: value
props.note: Held by the combobox, which changes it by a choice, a commit or the clear button; the combobox field's is the same at every moment (CBF-3).

props.name: inputValue
props.note: Held by the combobox, which writes it as the person types and when a value is chosen or restored; the combobox field's is the same at every moment (CBF-3).

props.name: label
props.note: Names the combobox. In a filled or outlined look the combobox draws it, floating in its box, and the Field draws no label row (FLD-25, CMB-8).

props.name: labelHidden
props.note: Hides the label wherever it would be drawn: the Field's row, or the combobox's floating label (FLD-25).

props.name: error
props.note: Puts the Field in its error condition, which puts the combobox in its own (FLD-8, CMB-10).

props.name: disabled
props.note: Disables the Field, which disables the combobox (FLD-14, CMB-46).

props.name: open
props.note: Held by the combobox, which opens and closes its list itself; the combobox field's is the same at every moment (CBF-3).

behavior.text: THE combobox field SHALL be a Field that frames one combobox, and nothing else. It SHALL give label, labelHidden, supportingText, errorText, error, disabled, required, optional, requiredMark, requiredText and optionalText to its Field and every other prop to its combobox, each unchanged; SHALL hold the label-icon slot for its Field and the leading-icon slot for its combobox; SHALL give its options to its combobox (CBF-2); and SHALL emit its combobox's events as its own, each once. THE combobox field SHALL be as wide as the place it stands in, and its combobox SHALL fill it: it is a block with no width of its own, as its Field is (FLD-1), around a control that fills the width it is given (CMB-49). It SHALL draw no part of its own and have no token of its own: what it shows, how it behaves and what it exposes to assistive technology SHALL be exactly what that Field and that combobox do when a product places the one in the other (FLD-1 to FLD-28; CMB-1 to CMB-62) — the label row and its requirement mark (FLD-2 to FLD-6), or the label that floats in the box with the Field's row left out (FLD-25, CMB-7, CMB-8); the supporting row and the error (FLD-7 to FLD-9, FLD-26, CMB-10); the name, the description and the states (FLD-10, FLD-11, FLD-14, CMB-12, CMB-46); and the list, which is the combobox's alone and as wide as its container (CMB-22).
behavior.verify: The twin test: every fixture of the combobox field has a twin, the Field's fixture combobox-<id>, a Field around a combobox written by hand with the same values and the same options; on every platform that draws both, the two are the same picture and the same accessibility tree. A difference is a finding in a member or in the exchange between them (CMB-61), never a baseline to update.

behavior.text: THE combobox field SHALL take the options and the option groups a product gives it — in the platform's form for a combobox's own (its child elements on the web) — and give them to its combobox as that combobox's options, in the order given, each with its label, its value, its supporting text, its leading icon and its disabled, and each group with its title: the option a product wrote SHALL be the option its combobox reads, never a copy of it. THE combobox field SHALL NOT read, filter, order, count or keep an option, and SHALL make no option active or chosen: which options are shown, which is active and which is the chosen one are its combobox's (CMB-25, CMB-26, CMB-36). WHEN the product adds, removes, reorders or changes an option or a group THE combobox field's combobox SHALL meet the change at once and as CMB-31 says, as though the product had changed that combobox's own options.
behavior.verify: Unit, on the web: `<tanrei-option>` children of the combobox field are the elements its combobox's rows are read from (the same element objects); appending a child, removing one, and changing a child's `label`, `disabled` and text each change the open list in the same turn as they do for a `<tanrei-combobox>` with the same children; with filter none, replacing every child from an `input` handler keeps the text being edited and the value (CMB-31).

behavior.text: THE combobox field SHALL hold no value, no text and no open state of its own: its value, its inputValue and its open SHALL at every moment be its combobox's. WHEN its combobox changes one of them — a choice, a commit or the clear button (CMB-17, CMB-20, CMB-27 to CMB-29); typing, or a text the combobox writes itself for a choice, for a commit that was given up or for Escape (CMB-16, CMB-27, CMB-29, CMB-30); the list opening or closing, or open taken back because there is nothing to show (CMB-21, CMB-30, CMB-57) — THE combobox field's SHALL be the new one before any event that reports the change is emitted, and equally WHERE no event reports it. WHEN the product sets one on the combobox field THE combobox field SHALL set it on its combobox and nothing else, so that no event follows (CMB-31).
behavior.verify: Unit, on the web, each read in the listener and after it: in an input listener on the combobox field, inputValue is the typed text; in a change listener, value and inputValue are the new ones; in a toggle listener, open is the new one. With allowCustomValue false and value "jp": type "kyo" and press Tab — no event fires, and the combobox field's inputValue is "Japan" again (CMB-29). Setting value, inputValue and open on the combobox field fires nothing.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has forms (the web) THE combobox field SHALL be the one control the form sees: it SHALL take name, submit its combobox's value — never the text of an edit that was not committed — reset to the value it was first given, restore it on navigation, report to the form's constraint validation exactly what its combobox would report there (CMB-59), and be left out WHILE disabled is true or a disabled group of the form holds it; its combobox and its Field SHALL take no part in the form themselves. WHEN Enter asks for the form's submission (CMB-28) the form asked SHALL be the combobox field's own, through that form's default button (BTN-30), and not WHEN action was cancelled.
behavior.verify: Unit, on the web: a form with one combobox field submits one entry under the field's name; reset and restore reach the combobox; required true with an empty value reports valueMissing on the combobox field and focuses its combobox's input when the form reports it; Enter with no option active presses the form's default button; an Enter that chooses an option submits nothing (CMB-27).

behavior.text: WHEN the combobox field is given focus — by the product, by a press on any part of it that FLD-12 or CMB-14 gives to the input, or by a form that reports its validity — THE combobox field SHALL pass the focus to its combobox's input and SHALL add no stop to the focus order: the stops inside it are its combobox's, in that combobox's order (the input, then the clear button while it is shown). WHILE focus is anywhere inside it, or its combobox's list is open, its Field's rows SHALL be drawn focused, because its combobox says so to its Field (FLD-13, CMB-61): the combobox field arranges nothing for it. A press on its Field's label row WHILE the list is open is a press outside the combobox: the list SHALL close with the reason outside, choosing nothing (CMB-30), and focus SHALL go to the input (FLD-12).

IF the combobox field is placed in a Field THE combobox field SHALL in debug builds report that it is a field already and that the bare control is the combobox, and both SHALL still render (FLD-15). WHILE it stands in a field group THE combobox field SHALL follow that group's disabled, through its own Field, and take nothing else from the group (FGR-20).

THE combobox field SHALL have no words of its own and SHALL read none: requiredText and optionalText are read by its Field (FLD-24), emptyText and clearLabel by its combobox (CMB-60), each from the instance's prop and then from the product's words.

WHERE the platform has ARIA attributes (the web), WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute on the host, by the attribute or by the ARIA property that reflects it, THE combobox field SHALL move it to the data-aria- attribute of the same name, so that the host is no second node with its name, description or state, and SHALL expose it on the element that carries its role — an id reference by the elements it names in the host's tree or a tree around it, an error message as part of the description while the combobox field is invalid — except those the combobox field owns (aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-disabled, aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, aria-controls), which it SHALL move and not expose: its name is label (CBF-1). WHEN the product removes the aria- attribute or its data-aria- twin, or sets the ARIA property that reflects it (ariaLabel, ariaDescribedByElements…) to null, THE combobox field SHALL take it off that element. WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute the combobox field owns THE combobox field SHALL report it in debug builds.

keyboard.action: The combobox's (its accessibility block; CMB-16, CMB-20, CMB-21, CMB-26 to CMB-30). The combobox field handles no key and adds no focus stop (CBF-5).

accessibility.labeling: The combobox field adds nothing to what its members expose and coordinates nothing: the Field gives the combobox its name, its description and its required, invalid and disabled states (FLD-8, FLD-10, FLD-11, FLD-14), and the combobox carries them on its own input, with its expanded state, its list and its active option (CMB-12, CMB-48). Assistive technology meets one editable combobox named by label, with a list of the same name, exactly as it meets a Field around a combobox written by hand.
notes: One level down is the same thing: a Field with a combobox in it, holding the same options. Every fixture has that pair as its twin, and the accessibility tree of the two is the same (CBF-1).

The options are the product's, and they are the combobox's: the combobox field passes them on and does nothing with them (CBF-2). Value, text and open are the combobox's too, and the combobox field keeps no second copy that could disagree with it (CBF-3).

On the web the two members stand in the combobox field's own shadow root, so the form meets the combobox field and not the combobox (CBF-4); focus passes through to the input (CBF-5); and the product's option elements stay its own children, read by the combobox through a slot.
A list is not a second thing the component reports: choosing an option is setting its one value, so the combobox field is composed, not a feature.

web.name: tanrei-combobox-field

option.name: tanrei-option
option.notes: `<tanrei-option value="tokyo">Tokyo</tanrei-option>`: the element a select holds, and the same data: the label is the `label` attribute or, without one, the element's text. Attributes `supporting-text`, `leading-icon`, `disabled`. It draws nothing itself. `tanrei-option` and `tanrei-option-group` are one pair of elements for the select and the combobox, defined once; an option with the empty value is refused by the combobox (CMB-17, CMB-57), not by the element, because a select allows it.

option-group.name: tanrei-option-group
option-group.notes: The title is the `label` attribute, as `<optgroup label>`: a `title` attribute would also draw the browser's tooltip.

web.notes: The tag `tanrei-combobox-field`, the class `TanreiComboboxField`, the React name `ComboboxField`. It takes the combobox's attributes, children and listeners and the Field's, name for name. The element is composed as every composed element on the web is (the web package's README, Composed elements); what follows is what is particular to it, and the three places where this element needs more than every composed element has. Members: `<tanrei-field>` holding one `<tanrei-combobox>` in its default slot; the product places no member. The host is `display: block`. Value member: `tanrei-combobox`. The host is the form's element — `name`, the value and its state, validity anchored on the combobox's input, reset to the `value` attribute, restore, `form`, a disabled fieldset — and the combobox inside has no `name`. Props, set as properties on the member each is from. On the Field: `label`, `labelHidden`, `supportingText`, `errorText`, `error`, `disabled`, `required`, `optional`, `requiredMark`, `requiredText`, `optionalText`. On the combobox: `variant`, `size`, `value`, `inputValue`, `placeholder`, `readOnly`, `open`, `allowCustomValue`, `filter`, `noChevron` (the inverse of `chevron`, attribute `no-chevron`), `clearable`, `clearLabel`, `status`, `statusText`, `emptyText`, `separation`. Attributes are the members' own: kebab-case, except `readonly`. Props of one name on both members — `label`, `labelHidden`, `error`, `disabled` — are the Field's; the combobox's are never set by the element and reach the combobox through the connection. **1. Three props the member writes** (a composed element sets each prop on its member, with one exception, the value, which it reads back on the member's event): the combobox writes `value`, `inputValue` and `open` itself, and writes the text with no event when a commit is given up (CMB-29). The host therefore keeps no copy of the three: each is an accessor over the member's property — a get reads the member's, a set writes the member's, and a value set before the member exists is kept and given at its first render — so that `event.target.value`, `.inputValue` and `.open` are the new ones in every listener and between events (CBF-3). `open` reflects on the host as it does on the member: the host writes its own attribute when the member tells it of an update, by the primitive through which the member already tells the host its form value. **2. The options are passed by the default slot** (other passed-on children use named slots): the shadow root is `<tanrei-field><slot name="label-icon" slot="label-icon"></slot><tanrei-combobox><slot></slot><slot name="leading-icon" slot="leading-icon"></slot></tanrei-combobox></tanrei-field>`. The product's `<tanrei-option>` and `<tanrei-option-group>` children stay the host's light-DOM children and are assigned to the unnamed `<slot>`, which is a child of the combobox; the combobox reads a `<slot>` among its children as the elements assigned to it and reads again on `slotchange` and on a change of an assigned element (`primitives/option-list.ts`, the combobox's web note; the select reads its options the same way, with the same reader). Unlike a passing named slot, the unnamed one is always rendered: the combobox draws no room for options, so an empty slot is no option. The host never reads its option children. Slots: `label-icon` is passed to the Field and `leading-icon` to the combobox, each by a slot element of the same name rendered only while the host has a child for it. **3. A forwarded attribute that is no prop**: `inline`, the combobox's web-only attribute that draws an open list in place for the fixtures, is forwarded as a property, and `select()` is passed on as `focus()` and `blur()` are. Events: `input` is the native, composed event of the text element, and `change` and `action` are the combobox's own composed, bubbling events; the three leave by themselves, with the host as their target, and `action` stays cancelable. `toggle` is composed and does not bubble: it is heard on the host, as on any shadow host, and by no ancestor — which needs the combobox's `toggle` to be composed, as it is not today (the combobox's web note). None is stopped and none is copied. Parts: the member hosts are `field` and `combobox`. Exported from the Field: `label`, `label-icon`, `requirement-label`, `supporting-text`. Exported from the combobox: `container`, `outline`, `active-indicator`, `label`, `requirement-label`, `input`, `leading-icon`, `clear-button`, `chevron`, `list`, `option`, `option-label`, `option-supporting-text`, `option-leading-icon`, `mark`, `group`, `group-title`, `divider`, `status`. Two names collide, `label` and `requirement-label`. Each is exported with its member's name before it, always (`field-label`, `combobox-label`, `field-requirement-label`, `combobox-requirement-label`), and under the bare name from both members as well, because the two are one thing to a person and are never drawn at once: FLD-25 is the sentence that holds it. Focus: the shadow root does not delegate. `focus()`, `blur()` and `select()` call the combobox's; a press on the label row focuses the input by FLD-12, a press on the box by CMB-14, and a press on the help does nothing. The combobox's list is a popover of the combobox's own shadow root, in the top layer; the combobox is its opener, so a press on the Field's rows while it is open is a press outside (CBF-5). The connection is the Field's with its control, with one value more upward, that the control is drawn focused (FLD-13, FLD-25, FLD-26, CMB-61); the element takes no part in it. Parts and tokens of its own: none. The element writes no custom property: `--tanrei-comp-field-*`, `--tanrei-comp-input-box-*` and `--tanrei-comp-combobox-*` reach the members by inheritance, and one combobox field is set apart by setting any of them on the element. What its twin cannot do that it does: nothing. The twin: `<tanrei-field label="City" supporting-text="Where the order is sent." required><tanrei-combobox name="city" value="tokyo"><tanrei-option value="kyoto">Kyoto</tanrei-option><tanrei-option value="tokyo">Tokyo</tanrei-option></tanrei-combobox></tanrei-field>`. Before the element is defined its options are running text: a page hides them with `tanrei-combobox-field:not(:defined) > * { display: none }` and gives the tag a block size. Words: none of its own; `required-text` and `optional-text` are read by the Field, `empty-text` and `clear-label` by the combobox.

swiftui.name: TanreiComboboxField
swiftui.notes: `TanreiComboboxField("City", selection: $city, text: $query) { TanreiComboboxOption("Tokyo").tag("tokyo") … }`: a view built from `TanreiField` and `TanreiCombobox`, with the combobox's two bindings and its content builder passed through and the Field's arguments beside them. It takes `TanreiCombobox`'s arguments, name for name. One instance is set apart by `.tanreiTheme(_:)` on the view. The options are `TanreiComboboxOption` and `TanreiComboboxSection`, the combobox's own. Planned, after the Field and the combobox.

option.notes: `TanreiComboboxOption(text, value, supportingText, leadingIcon, enabled)`, called in the combobox's content lambda.

compose.notes: `TanreiComboboxField(value, onValueChange, label = "City") { TanreiComboboxOption("Tokyo", "tokyo") … }`: a composable that calls `TanreiField` with `TanreiCombobox` as its content and passes the content lambda through. `enabled` is the inverse flag and `isError` keeps Compose's name. One instance is set apart by `TanreiTheme(…) { }` around it. Planned, after the Field and the combobox.

flutter.notes: `TanreiComboboxField(value:, onChanged:, labelText:, helperText:, errorText:, options: […])`: a widget that builds `TanreiField` around `TanreiCombobox` and passes `options` through; `labelText`, `hintText`, `helperText`, `errorText` and `enabled` keep `InputDecoration`'s names, `enabled` the inverse flag. `TanreiComboboxFormField` wraps the combobox field as a `FormField<String>`. One instance is set apart by a `TanreiTheme` around it. Planned, after the Field and the combobox.

react-native.notes: `<ComboboxField label="City" supportingText="Where the order is sent." value={city} onValueChange={setCity} options={[…]} />`: a component that renders `Field` around `Combobox` and passes `options` through as given. `inputValue` / `onInputValueChange` and `open` / `onOpenChange` are the combobox's optional pairs. One instance is set apart by a provider around it. Planned, after the Field and the combobox.
